title: Study OS
tagline: When it doesn't click, change the explanation
description: A public AI learning project exploring a new market gap: models can generate endless explanations, but learners still need help finding the one that makes sense to them. Study OS learns from where a student gets stuck, tries a different representation, and keeps the evidence tied to real learning sessions.

title: Cortex
tagline: A reliability kernel for AI agents
description: Coding agents are capable, but you can't trust their output without reviewing it, and reviewing costs about what the work did. So I inverted the usual bet: instead of a smarter agent, build the machinery around it. A deny-by-default reference monitor, unforgeable content-bound receipts, trust-graded sandboxes, and deterministic oracle gates let interchangeable models do real work on a codebase you never have to read to trust. It composes decades-proven OS-security patterns into a trust kernel for agent software production, built contract-first and self-hosting: every module ships through the same gates it will one day enforce.

title: FOSSIL
description: Preserves the research, evidence, rejected paths and changing reasoning behind human-led technical decisions so the reason for a choice stays inspectable months later.

title: ONI vs My Agent Ready Architecture
description: Software architecture has not caught up with agent-first coding yet. I built an npm package so repos keep agent speed without losing planning time, audit trails, or architecture shape — modular boundaries, contracts, versioned dev logs, agent-readable JSON audits, prompt versioning, evals, and patch/rollback context stronger than git alone. Inspired by Oxygen Not Included systems thinking; tested with multi-agent pipelines up to 500 agents and designed to grow naturally toward microservices.

title: Ekagajpatra
description: Built a civic-tech product that turned complex government and legal-documentation processes into guided workflows for real users.

title: SaaS Dashboard Systems
description: Built dashboards, analytics views, workflow prototypes, and client-specific tools for legal, financial, and business operations teams.

title: Legal Workflow Research
description: Independent research into safer AI-assisted legal workflows using document intelligence, confidence routing, source authority, human review, and procedural memory.

title: Fluffy V4
description: Fluffy is an agent workflow that researches a product, its buyers, market and proof before it writes any marketing, then renders several genuinely different directions for a human to judge. V4 is an eight-direction review gallery covering Fluffy itself and two pilot products, and it is now being rebuilt one page at a time with a reference-first visual pipeline.

title: Eval Lab
tagline: When should we trust the judge?
description: A reproducible research lab for lightweight AI judges. It compares judge decisions with objective evidence such as answer keys, deterministic verifiers and executable tests, checks whether confidence is calibrated, and studies when an uncertain case should escalate to a stronger judge or a person. Selective escalation is still an active research direction.

title: Project Continuity Modules
description: A protocol and a small Python CLI (continuity) that keep a project's working memory in Git as plain Markdown and JSON: what the project is, where it stands, the active task and the last checkpoint, so any fresh human or agent session can resume the work. Source-only for now; not a replacement for Git or a hosted memory service.

title: Inference Recommendation Engine
tagline: The lowest price is not the decision
description: A local, provider-neutral engine that ranks inference routes from price ladders, observed supply, runtime evidence and an editable, versioned policy. It returns deterministic scores, evidence status and gate reasons so a recommendation can be inspected and reproduced. It is a small core package, not a hosted router.
